approach: Linear expansion makes the scale misread away from 25°C; find the temperature change producing the 0.5 mm allowed error, then apply it on both sides of 25°C.

steps.text: Write the length of the scale and the maximum allowed error in the same unit.
steps.equation: L = 1000 mm, allowed error δ = 0.5 mm

steps.text: Use the linear expansion relation to find the temperature change that produces this error.
steps.why_this_step: The scale's marked length changes by Lα ΔT for a temperature change ΔT away from the temperature at which it was made.

steps.text: The scale reads correctly to within 0.5 mm whether it is heated above 25°C (it expands and under-reads) or cooled below 25°C (it contracts and over-reads), so this 50°C limit applies on both sides of 25°C.

common_mistakes.text: Assuming the scale only goes wrong when heated above 25°C, and forgetting it also errs when cooled below 25°C, gives the one-sided range +25°C to +75°C.
Treating the calculated 50°C as the width of the whole allowed range instead of the deviation on each side, and splitting it as ±25°C about 25°C, gives 0°C to +50°C.
